result.summary: Reject empty overflow pages as corruption when parsing read-only Berkeley DB files in BerkeleyRODatabase::Open. This prevents an infinite loop when an overflow page with zero data links back to itself or another empty page.
result.problem: When reading BDB overflow records, the parser terminates only when next_page is 0 or when total read bytes exceed item_len. An overflow page with no data (hf_offset of 0) adds zero bytes to the accumulator, so a cycle of empty pages causes migratewallet or bitcoin-wallet dump to spin indefinitely at 100% CPU on an HTTP worker thread and blocks node shutdown.
evidence: PR description measurements demonstrate bitcoin-wallet dump spinning at 100% of a core until killed after 60s on master when encountering an empty self-referential overflow page, whereas it fails immediately with this PR.

PR description notes that running migratewallet against such a file causes the RPC to never return, leaves one HTTP worker at 100% CPU, and prevents clean shutdown (bitcoind stop did not finish after 30s).
result.changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete implementation diff and functional test in tool_wallet.py; the approach and logic are unchanged.
result.card: Reject empty overflow pages as database corruption in the read-only Berkeley DB parser. When an overflow page contains no data and points back to itself, parsing loops indefinitely, pinning a CPU core at 100% and hanging wallet migration or dump operations as well as node shutdown. Author measurements show master spinning until killed while this PR fails immediately, backed by a new functional test.

risk.why: A false positive could fail to read or migrate a legacy BDB wallet, but valid BDB files do not produce empty overflow pages.
